title: Linking incident RCA to shipping gates: PRD updates for KV-cache regeneration and regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Following a production incident where KV-cache rehydration frequently stalled under tail load, this ticket captures PRD-level requirement changes that map the post-incident action items into concrete shipping gates, acceptance criteria, and scope adjustments. Goal is to ensure future releases do not regress runtime behavior and that operational teams can detect and remediate cache-stall regressions before customer-visible SLOs are impacted.

Background: The incident RCA identified three contributing causes: non-deterministic cache rehydrate ordering causing KV conflicts, insufficient synthetic coverage for long-tail sequence lengths, and unclear rollback/runbook acceptance criteria for canary rollouts that allow unhealthy kernels to progress to 100% traffic. Existing PRD language around cache rehydration and rollout gating is underspecified.

What this ticket changes in the PRD: 1) Add an explicit verification matrix for KV-cache rehydrate paths (happy path, concurrent writes, partial eviction). 2) Require synthetic long-tail workload scenarios in CI that exercise sequence lengths >5k tokens and cache churn. 3) Define rollout gates: canary traffic % steps, minimum telemetry signals required (tail latency, cache miss surge, regen rate), and automatic abort criteria tied to SLO delta. 4) Add runbook acceptance tests: simulated cache-stall injected chaos + automated traffic shepherding verification. 5) Add observability deliverables: dashboards, alert thresholds, and a short list of traces/metrics for oncall.

Scope decisions: We will not require a full kernel redesign in this PRD update; engineering can deliver mitigations (ordering guards, small rehydrate backoff, and KV priming heuristics) in this release with a follow-on project for kernel-level KV correctness. The PRD will call out that kernel-level work is required for long-term mitigation and reference a follow-up epic.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout policy defined in config and verified: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated hold of at least 15 minutes at each step
Telemetry signals required for progressing canary: tail P99 latency <= baseline + 15ms AND cache-miss-rate delta < 2x baseline AND KV-regen-rate stable
Automated abort triggers: if any required telemetry exceeds thresholds for two consecutive collection windows, canary automatically rolls back and opens incident runbook
Synthetic verification: CI job that runs the long-tail synthetic workload reproduces the cache-rehydrate scenario without retries failing more than 1% of requests across 3 consecutive runs
Runbook acceptance: invoking the 'KV-cache rehydrate stall' runbook in staging executes automated traffic shepherding and results in restored normal throughput within 10 minutes in 90% of test runs
Dashboards and alerts: per-route dashboard created, alerted on P99 tail latency and cache-miss surge; alert runbook linked and validated by SRE
Security: any changes to cache encryption keys or KMS usage documented and passed security review before release
